title: Finite Zariski gluing of admissible module flatifications
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}V_\alpha$ be a finite cover by quasi-compact open subschemes. For each $\alpha$, fix a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J_\alpha\subset\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}$ equal to the unit ideal on $U\cap V_\alpha$, such that the module strict transform of $\mathcal F|_{X\times_SV_\alpha}$ under $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_\alpha}V_\alpha\to V_\alpha$ is flat over $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_\alpha}V_\alpha$.

There exist finite-type quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal L_\alpha\subset\mathcal O_S$ with $\mathcal L_\alpha|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal L_\alpha|_{V_\alpha}=\mathcal J_\alpha$. For such extensions, put $\mathcal L=\prod_\alpha\mathcal L_\alpha$ (the empty product is $\mathcal O_S$). The blowup $b:S^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}S\to S$ is $U$-admissible and factors through every $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_\alpha}S$ as a further admissible blowup, whose centre is the extension of $\prod_{\beta\ne\alpha}\mathcal L_\beta$. On $b^{-1}V_\alpha$ this is the corresponding two-step blowup starting with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_\alpha}V_\alpha$. The restriction of the global module strict transform $\mathcal F^b$ is canonically the successive module strict transform along this factorization, compatibly with the quotient from ordinary pullback, and is flat over $b^{-1}V_\alpha$. Consequently $\mathcal F^b$ is flat over $S^b$. Schemes, qcqs conventions, quasi-coherence, relative module flatness, admissible blowups, module strict transforms, fibre products and module pullbacks are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. Blowups themselves are those of [def-nagata-global-blowup].

source.place: Tags 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 1, and 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph: extending and dominating local blowups. Returned proof step 9.

proof.text: For each $\alpha$, glue $\mathcal J_\alpha$ on $V_\alpha$ with $\mathcal O_U$ on $U$ by [lemma-nagata-glue-finite-type-ideals]: their restrictions to $U\cap V_\alpha$ are equal by hypothesis. This produces a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal H_\alpha$ on $W_\alpha=U\cup V_\alpha$. The finite union $W_\alpha$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension-exists] to the qcqs scheme $S$, the quasi-compact open $W_\alpha$, and $\mathcal H_\alpha$. Its extension $\mathcal L_\alpha$ has precisely the two required restrictions. No compatibility between different $\mathcal J_\alpha$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 080M, lemma-extend-admissible-blowups, proof; properties.tex Tag 01PF, lemma-extend

proof.text: Fix any such extensions, and set $\mathcal L=\prod_\alpha\mathcal L_\alpha$ and $\mathcal M_\alpha=\prod_{\beta\ne\alpha}\mathcal L_\beta$. These are finite-type quasi-coherent ideals: on an affine open their ideals are generated by the finite lists of products of generators of the factors; localization preserves these products. Their restrictions to $U$ are the unit ideal. Thus $b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}S\to S$ is $U$-admissible by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Empty products have the generator $1$.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 080N, lemma-dominate-admissible-blowups, product of ideals

proof.text: For each $\alpha$, use [thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal] with the two ideals $\mathcal L_\alpha,\mathcal M_\alpha$. The iterated blowup meant by that theorem is specified in [def-nagata-blowup-product-comparison]: first blow up $\mathcal L_\alpha$, then its extended $\mathcal M_\alpha$. Since $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_\alpha\mathcal M_\alpha$, the theorem gives the required global factorization of $b$. On the inverse image of $U$, the second centre is the extension of the unit ideal, hence is the unit ideal. It is finite type (the images of a finite local generating family generate the extended ideal), Write $b_\alpha:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_\alpha}S\to S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] the open $b_\alpha^{-1}U$ is the fibre product $U\times_S\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_\alpha}S$; the inclusion $U\to S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) ($U$ quasi-compact, $S$ quasi-separated), so its base change $b_\alpha^{-1}U\to\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_\alpha}S$ is a quasi-compact open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Hence this second blowup is $b_\alpha^{-1}U$-admissible by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup].

Apply [lem-trf-factorized-centres-product-transform] with index set $A$, $T_\alpha=V_\alpha$, $Y_\alpha=X\times_SV_\alpha$, the open inclusions $e_\alpha:T_\alpha\to S$, $j_\alpha:Y_\alpha\to X$, and ideals $\mathcal I_\alpha=\mathcal L_\alpha$, $\mathcal J_\alpha$ as given, $\mathcal J'_\alpha=\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}$. Check the hypotheses: $T_\alpha$ is quasi-compact by assumption and quasi-separated as an open of $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $Y_\alpha=X\times_SV_\alpha$ is the open subscheme $f^{-1}V_\alpha$ of $X$, with $j_\alpha$ its inclusion and $g_\alpha$ the restriction of $f$. The open inclusions $e_\alpha,j_\alpha$ identify their source local rings with the corresponding target local rings, so are flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. The map $e_\alpha$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since its source is quasi-compact and its target quasi-separated. The square commutes by the fibre-product projections. Finally $\mathcal I_\alpha\mathcal O_{T_\alpha}=\mathcal L_\alpha|_{V_\alpha}=\mathcal J_\alpha\mathcal J'_\alpha$, and the first strict transform is flat by the given hypothesis on the blowup of $V_\alpha$ in $\mathcal J_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph; Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, product-centre comparison

proof.text: The conclusion of [lem-trf-factorized-centres-product-transform] now has $\mathcal K_\alpha=\prod_{\beta\ne\alpha}(\mathcal L_\beta|_{V_\alpha})=\mathcal M_\alpha|_{V_\alpha}$ and $T_\alpha^b=b^{-1}V_\alpha$. It identifies the restriction of $b$ there with the two-step blowup starting at $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_\alpha}V_\alpha$, and the restriction of $\mathcal F^b$ with the successive module strict transform, commuting with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps. Its last clause says this successive transform is the ordinary pullback of the first, flat transform and is flat over $b^{-1}V_\alpha$. These are exactly the local comparison and flatness claims; no scheme strict-transform lemma is substituted for the module assertion.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph; Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize; divisors.tex Tags 080I (1) and 080F (2)

proof.text: The opens $b^{-1}V_\alpha$ cover $S^b$, since the $V_\alpha$ cover $S$. For any $z\in X\times_SS^b$, choose $\alpha$ with its image $t\in S^b$ in $b^{-1}V_\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (twice) $b^{-1}V_\alpha=V_\alpha\times_SS^b=T_\alpha^b$ and $Y_\alpha\times_SS^b=Y_\alpha\times_{T_\alpha}T_\alpha^b$ is the open preimage of $b^{-1}V_\alpha$ in $X\times_SS^b$, which contains $z$. Restricting to these opens changes neither $\mathcal F^b_z$ nor $\mathcal O_{S^b,t}$. The local flatness just proved therefore says that $\mathcal F^b_z$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S^b,t}$. The stalk characterization in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] proves global relative flatness. If $A$ is empty, its being a cover forces $S$ and hence $X$ and $S^b$ to be empty; the product ideal is the unit ideal and all pointwise flatness assertions are vacuous. This also covers empty members of a nonempty cover.
